title: The Tab Order & Keyboard Fundamentals ⌨️
description: Understand how focus works, how the browser determines tab order, and the dangers of tabindex.

slides.title: Keyboard Accessibility: The Backbone of Interaction 💪
slides.content:
Many users rely entirely on the keyboard – motor‑impaired, blind users with screen readers, power users. If an interface isn't keyboard‑accessible, it's broken.

Key principles:
- All functionality must be available using a keyboard (WCAG 2.1.1).
- The focus order must be logical and predictable (WCAG 2.4.3).
- Users must never get trapped in a component.

Think of it like driving a car: you need steering, accelerator, brakes – all within reach. Keyboard is the steering wheel of the web.

quizData.question: Which WCAG criterion requires all functionality to be operable through a keyboard interface?
quizData.explanation: Success Criterion 2.1.1 (Level A) mandates keyboard operability.

slides.title: Understanding Focus 🎯
slides.content:
Focus is the browser's way of saying "this element is ready to receive input".

- Only one element can have focus at a time.
- Interactive elements (links, buttons, inputs, select, textarea) are focusable by default.
- Non‑interactive elements (div, span, p) are not.

You can make any element focusable using the `tabindex` attribute – but with great power comes great responsibility.

slides.title: Focusable Elements
slides.codeSnippet:
Plain div
I'm focusable now

quizData.question: Which element is natively focusable?
quizData.explanation: Links with an href attribute are focusable by default.

slides.title: Tab Order & DOM Order 📖
slides.content:
By default, the tab order follows the **DOM order** (source order). Elements are focused in the sequence they appear in the HTML.

- Always ensure visual order matches DOM order.
- CSS flexbox/grid can visually reorder things – but focus still follows the DOM. This can be disorienting.

**Golden rule**: make the DOM order logical and then style it.

quizData.question: If you use CSS `order` to move a nav to the top, what happens to the keyboard tab order?

options.text: It also moves to the top
It stays in the original DOM order

quizData.explanation: Keyboard tab order always reflects DOM order, not visual order.

slides.title: The `tabindex` Attribute: Use Sparingly ⚠️
slides.content:
`tabindex` values:

- **`-1`** – element is programmatically focusable (with JS) but NOT in the natural tab order. Used for focus management (e.g., modals).
- **`0`** – element becomes focusable and is placed in the natural tab order based on DOM position.
- **Positive values (1, 2, 3...)** – **AVOID!** They create a custom tab order that's hard to maintain and disorienting.

Only use `tabindex="0"` or `tabindex="-1"`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Never use `tabindex="1"` or higher
It can create a 'tab index race' that's impossible to debug. Use DOM order instead.
